Subject: Request — Isolation & traffic attenuation diagrams for Dedicated/Private

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this. Greenline's security team (Marco Ruiz copied) is working through the SIG/SOC2 pack and they asked for a clear architecture overview showing how Redwood enforces tenant isolation and limits cross-tenant broadcast/side-channel risk in Dedicated and Private deployments. The specific asks are: 

- A network diagram that shows control plane vs data plane boundaries, peering, and any overlay/VRF-like constructs used to prevent tenant traffic leakage.
- A short explanation of how we attenuate noisy/side-effect traffic (e.g., ARP/ND, broadcast discovery, metadata service exposure) between tenants.
- Evidence pointers: exported flow logs, egress chokepoint design, and where audit logs/KMS boundaries live.

Can you provide a diagram (PDF/PNG) and a short Q&A by EOD Friday? Marco also asked for a 30-minute call to walk the team through the diagram.

Appreciate it — if you want a template we can drop our SIG question list in the Drive link.

Best,
Ava Santos
Security Program Manager
Ava Solutions (for Greenline AI)

Thanks — looping in Soojin and Jonas from Security Architecture. We can deliver a compact diagram and an evidence bundle that answers the SIG/SOC2 questions. Plan:

- Attached: initial tenant-attenuation-diagram-v2.png (visual overview) and control-matrix-tenant-isolation.xlsx (controls mapped to SIG/CATs).
- Follow-up note: we will include exported VPC flow log snippets and a short egress-logging playbook as additional evidence in one consolidated zip.
- Proposed next step: 30-minute walkthrough Thursday 08/05 at 10:00 PT — does that work?

Quick summary of what the diagram will highlight (so the reviewers know what to look for):
- Strict control plane separation: customer management/control plane lives in a locked management VNET with dedicated ENIs and never shares tenant data plane subnets.
- Tenant overlays: per-tenant overlay networks (VRF-like) with policy-based routing; we term this our "attenuation overlay" to emphasize suppression of broad discovery traffic.
- Egress chokepoints: all tenant outbound flows traverse regional egress gateways with tag-based firewalling and mandatory flow logging retained per account for 180 days.

I'll add a short note explaining the "attenuation" mechanisms below the diagram. If that preliminary diagram looks good we'll finalize PDF export and drop the evidence bundle into the Drive link.

Best,

Hi all — adding a few concrete notes to accompany the diagram so the reviewers have context before the walkthrough.

Attenuation model (short):
- Non-broadcast tenancy: tenants are placed in isolated L3 overlays. We avoid flat L2 constructs that enable ARP/ND propagation. The overlay enforces per-tenant forwarding tables; any broadcast/multicast at the hypervisor/edge is dropped at the tenant boundary.
- Control plane segregation: control-plane agents (orchestration API, autoscaling controllers) run in a separate management VNET with one-way service endpoints into tenant domains. Management never injects tenant data into its telemetry streams.
- Inference-sidecar boundary: for Dedicated and Private we terminate tenant-facing proxies in per-tenant sidecars that enforce request-scoped policies (rate limits, header stripping, metadata access controls). Sidecars refuse any inbound traffic that lacks tenant-specific X-Tenant headers or mTLS-derived identity.
- Egress attenuation & chokepoint: all outbound traffic routes through regional egress gateways (NAT+L7 firewall), which apply allowlists and tag-based routing. This provides a single place for DLP, egress logging, and TLS inspection. Flow logs (VPC flow logs, NSG logs) are pushed to a segregated logging account and retained for 180 days by default; export to the customer's SIEM is supported by request.
- KMS & key boundary: tenant encryption keys are stored in a customer-isolated KMS partition for Private deployments, and a logically separated key namespace in Dedicated. We include the KMS boundary on slide 2 of the diagram.

Evidence pointers (what we'll include):
- Sample VPC flow log excerpts showing deny/no-cross-tenant flows.
- Firewall/NAT config snapshot for the regional egress gateway.
- Sidecar policy YAML snippets (redacted).
- Audit log table showing admin access into the management VNET (timestamped).

Notes on 'attenuation' term: we use this to emphasize proactive suppression of discovery/noise (not only enforcement after a leak). Practically, attenuation = drop broadcast/multicast, restrict metadata access, and centralize egress inspection.

Attaching a short playbook (egress-logging-playbook.pdf) with retention and SIEM export steps.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Security Architect — Redwood Inference
